As I am of legal age and have drank "craft" beers before, I never really got into it. I only have tried mainstream beers that claim to be awesome and some are. Anyway, I am looking for a new hobby and IDK if craft beer is something I would or wouldn't like, but am willing to give a try. Am wondering your guys opinion on a great first beer to start out with to try.

The best way to get into craft beers is by going to a beer fest. You get a small glass and unlimited samples. There are usually a good supply of brewers available and each brewer typical brings a couple different beers. Most fests we go to have 100+ different beers to sample.

What is so eye opening about a beerfest is you get to try so many different styles, usually at 2 ozs per pour, so you can try everything. If you don't like something, two swallows and its gone, off to find something better. If you do like something, often there are brewery reps right there pouring you beer so you can talk to someone who is happy to tell you all about their beer. Ask them about what style it is to give you an idea of what to keep an eye out for later. Sometimes they can even give you an overview of the hop profile and grain bill, but that is a bit advanced for someone just starting out. If you are feeling bold you can ask them to suggest some other breweries at the event you may be insterested in given that fact that you liked what they were serving. Also ask for what styles are similar that you may like. I have found that the brewery reps love talking about their beer and will be happy to give you whatever info they find may be helpful to a new craft beer drinker.

So now you have had a taste of something you really like, and have been told it is style XYZ. Well the good news is there are more than likely other brewers with that same style. Visit the other tables, ask them what they have on tap, and give some a try. By the end you should hopefully walk away with a list of styles you find interesting and a list of breweries who you want to try more of their brews.
